title: Predictive mini-batching + kernel-probe guardrails to reduce embedding p99
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Reduce 99th-percentile latency for the embeddings endpoint by combining a predictive mini-batching scheduler with a low-overhead kernel-probe mechanism. The goal is to lower embed p99 by at least 35% for mixed small/large request workloads while keeping median latency impact <= 10% and avoiding increased tail in other endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: p99 for embeddings API decreases by >= 35% in the mixed traffic perf benchmark (synthetic mix of small single-vec and batched requests)
median latency (p50) increases by <= 10% vs baseline for same throughput
no regressions in throughput for large bulk-batch flows (>= 95% of baseline QPS)
feature gated rollout with telemetry dashboards and automated rollback on p99 spike
end-to-end integration tests and perf harness in CI reproducing target workload
implementation_plan: Design predictive mini-batching scheduler: use short horizon request arrival prediction (exponential weighted moving average of inter-arrival times) to trigger opportunistic micro-batches for small requests

Add kernel-probe shim in runtime: before committing to a kernel path, run a sub-millisecond probe to estimate expected kernel latency for the current key-value cache state and seq-len; probe must be non-blocking and limit probes per-GPU to avoid noise
Implement guardrails: if probe indicates a high-variance kernel choice or long latency, prefer small-instance fast-path or fall back to degrader model variant (quantized) depending on policy
Integrate with existing dispatch queue and priority stack; expose per-route knobs for predictive window and probe budget
Instrument detailed telemetry: per-request batch-size, predicted vs actual wait time, probe result, chosen kernel, backend latency components (queue, kernel, memcpy)
Create local perf harness that simulates live mix (70% single, 20% micro-batch of 4, 10% bulk) and run A/B against baseline kernels
Run gradual rollout on dedicated canary cluster with synthetic traffic and a subset of production real traffic (5%); monitor dashboards and automated alarms
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime config: predictive_mini_batching = off by default
Stage 1: internal perf cluster with deterministic load (1d)
Stage 2: dedicated canary region 5% of production QPS (3d) with automatic rollback threshold: embedding p99 > baseline * 1.15
Stage 3: increase to 25% with manual review of telemetry (5d)
Stage 4: global rollout with monitoring and escalation runbook
metrics: Secondary: embed_api_p50_latency_ms, embed_qps, embed_error_rate, kernel_probe_count_per_min, probe_error_rate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: probe overhead increases median latency -> Mitigation: limit probe budget per-GPU and make probe asynchronous with conservative backoff
Risk: mispredicted batching causes head-of-line blocking for large requests -> Mitigation: priority-aware scheduling that always favors in-flight large-batch drains; bounded wait time for singletons
Risk: kernel-probe interacts poorly with quantized fallback and causes oscillation -> Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum dwell time before switching kernel families
Risk: added complexity hides failures -> Mitigation: add visibility in Console: per-node probe success ratio, kernel handoff rate, and exploded traces for top tail contributors
